decision: Retry only transient incident failures within one finite shared session/retry budget, preserving the original POST key and serialized body. Continue location manually on invalid data, timeout, 429 or offline; only validated provider results enter the volatile TTL cache. Report terminal/conflict/unconfirmed outcomes explicitly and retain durable W08 intent until an exact receipt confirms it. Application owns policy and Infrastructure owns transport/timers; App.tsx injects the actual graph.
alternatives: Retry every transient call independently in UI, session and workspace: appears convenient but multiplies sends, loses a total budget and can duplicate POST effects after a lost response; rejected in favor of one incident request executor.

Fail immediately and forbid manual location or write replay: reduces network load but makes provider availability block incident reporting and leaves a committed timeout hard to recover; rejected in favor of manual location and explicit stable replay.

Centralize retries in the HTTP incident executor with injected clock and policy, isolate Photon cooldown/cache/manual lookup, and retain W08 confirmation semantics: chosen for replaceable providers, deterministic verification and bounded recovery.
tradeoff: Benefit: useful manual reporting during provider failures, bounded network load, preserved session isolation and one effect after replay. Cost: at most four sends per logical request (up to eight for separate sync read/write), finite latency, volatile cache after restart, public Photon without SLA, and explicit human retry/review when no exact receipt arrives. Never shorten a valid Retry-After to fit the cap; stop instead.
